# Build plan — the ticket board

**Contents:** [Where to start](#where-to-start) · [How to read a ticket](#how-to-read-a-ticket) · [Skeleton auth](#-one-named-build-time-decision--skeleton-auth) · [Building for V1](#building-for-v1) · [Beyond V1 — the deferred register](#beyond-v1--the-deferred-register)

> **The destination is [v1.md](v1.md)** — the first pilot, and the thing every open ticket is for. **Closed work lives in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md)** (the walking-skeleton milestones M0–M6, the Phase 7 QA batch, Slices A–A2.6, the UI-polish batch); **design rulings live in the ADRs, and their reasoning in [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md)**; **open questions live in [grill-questions.md](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md)** as `Q-###`. This board carries only tickets and the design a ticket needs to be built against.
>
> **Standing conventions.** **When a ticket closes (✅), its record moves to [plan-history.md](plan-history.md) in the same commit**, and a struck one-line pointer stays here — title, outcome, migration if there was one, and the link. When a question is ruled, its record moves to grill-history.md in the same commit. When an area is built, its design reference block folds into its component doc — see [the fold-in register](#the-fold-in-register) below.
>
> ⚖ **The move runs at TICKET grain, changed 2026-08-28 from slice grain.** The old rule — a slice's block moves when the *slice* closes — worked while slices closed in a day and quietly failed when they stopped. Slice Ask had been part-closed for four weeks, so its 22 finished tickets could never move and its record grew here for ever: **52% of this board was work already done**, 135 KB of it, and none of it was anybody forgetting the rule. Ticket grain is the same convention the [question tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md) has always used — a ruled question leaves a struck line and its record goes to the history.
>
> **Enforced** by `pnpm run check:board` (`scripts/board-rules.mjs`), locally and in CI: a closed entry anywhere above [the deferred register](#beyond-v1--the-deferred-register) — [Where to start](#where-to-start) included, since 2026-08-28's audit found the frontier regrowing the archive above the guard's old ceiling — that runs to more than one line, or that does not point at plan-history.md, or whose number is not actually in the history, fails the build. The prose version of this rule is the one that just spent four weeks not happening.
>
> **Nothing is summarised on the way out.** A record moves verbatim: the value of an entry is the finding in it, and a finding compressed on filing is a finding lost.

> **Status: execution, live.** This board answers two questions and no more: **what is being built for V1** (the live slices below, sequenced by [v1.md](v1.md)'s waypoints) and **what is deferred but still recorded** (the roadmap slices, each naming its gate; the 🌫 fog; the [tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md)). Method context, cited once: this is the [7-phases method](https://www.aihero.dev/my-7-phases-of-ai-development)'s execution board — its phases 1–4 produced the design layer (overview, the Legora reference, and the PRD trio of the walking-skeleton spec — closed, removed 2026-08-04, record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md) — + [data-model.md](data-model.md) + [contracts.md](contracts.md)); its phase 5 planned it; execution works it; the QA pass raises new tickets here. The walking skeleton is **built and closed**; the current horizon is **[v1.md](v1.md)**.
>
> **Scope discipline:** a slice is ticketed when it starts, not before — post-V1 slices below are a roadmap only, matching the data model's drawer-by-drawer rule. The board lives in this file for now; export to GitHub Issues when we want agents working it in parallel.

## How to read a ticket

`T-###` — title. **Next free number: T-393** — **derive it, don't trust it: `pnpm run check:tickets -- --next`** scans this board, the history *and* `git log` and prints the next free number. Bump this line in the same commit that claims numbers; `pnpm run check` fails if it falls behind, or if one number is defined twice. The line stays because it is readable, but the script is the authority — the prose convention alone let concurrent sessions collide twice (T-208–T-210, T-223–T-233). **Deps:** tickets that must be done first — **tickets only, never a `Q-###`** (see the rule below).

**⚖ The Q/T boundary — what earns a ticket number** *(adopted 2026-08-01)*. **A `T-###` is minted when the work can be *specified*. A `Q-###` exists when the question can be *stated*.** Being able to state a question precisely is not the same as being able to answer it, and it is never enough to justify a build ticket. So: unruled work is named in its slice's prose as **🌫 Fog** and ticketed when the ruling lands; a Deps field contains tickets only; and **what a question blocks lives in that question's own Blocks field**, which is the one place that relationship is recorded. The cost of getting this wrong is not theoretical — tickets minted against open questions carried the tracker's *recommendations* into their text, and when the rulings went the other way the board contradicted itself and needed a reconciliation commit (504f473). **Done when:** the acceptance test, drawn from the destination spec its slice serves — [v1.md](v1.md) for current work, [plan-history.md](plan-history.md) for the closed skeleton milestones. Package names from [repo-structure.md](repo-structure.md). A ticket is sized for one focused agent run (roughly a PR each).

**Definition of done, every ticket:** typed against `packages/contracts`; unit-tested; no surface reaches below the API; no code path resolves its own permissions (component 2 rule); lints and builds clean in CI.

**🗺 The board's vocabulary — one word per concept** *(adopted 2026-08-04, the way the Q/T boundary was — a board convention, not an ADR)*. Five overlapping taxonomies had accumulated — method phases, v1.md's own "phases", slices, waves, the skeleton's milestones — and the fix is definition and retirement, never re-sequencing: every dependency, marker and gate means precisely what it meant before. The metaphor is the [Wayfinder method's](https://www.aihero.dev/skills-wayfinder), which this board had three-quarters adopted on its own — *destination*, *frontier* and *fog* were already the legend's words.

- **The destination** — [v1.md](v1.md): what "done" looks like for the current horizon. One at a time; the previous one (the walking skeleton) closed into the history.
- **Waypoint** — the destination's own internal sequencing: v1.md's **Waypoint A** (the pilot floor), **B** (the agent made real), **C** (the product surface). Renamed from "Phase A/B/C" so the word "phase" stops meaning two things.
- **Slice** — a named, permanent grouping of tickets that ships together (`Slice V1-S`, `Slice Ask`, …). Slice ids are identifiers, never renumbered. A slice may carry **slice-local sublabels** — Slice Ask's Waves 0–8, and **parts** (written `P1`–`P4`; the P reads "part") in the co-authoring and ontology slices — read them as that slice's private chapter numbers and nothing wider.
- **Slice ids are keys, not names** *(adopted 2026-08-05)*. Like ticket numbers: permanent, unique, and not how prose talks. Running text leads with the name and carries the key in parens — "the ontology slice (O), part 2", never "Slice O P2". **The letter era is closed**: future slices take word names ("Slice Checker"), so no new decoder ring grows, and the letters stop colliding with Waypoints A–C.
- **Deferred work is a register entry, not a slice** *(adopted 2026-08-05)*. A capability not being built this iteration gets one entry in [Beyond V1 — the deferred register](#beyond-v1--the-deferred-register) — its gate pointed at (never restated from the tracker), its design named. It becomes a slice with tickets only when its gate clears, in the same commit that deletes its register entry.
- **The four states** — ▶ Frontier · ⏳ Sequenced · 🌫 Fog · 🚧 Gate, defined in [Where to start](#where-to-start).
- **Two kinds of ticket, deliberately.** A `Q-###` resolves a **decision** (Wayfinder's tickets are exactly this); a `T-###` builds a **specified thing** (the downstream work Wayfinder hands to `/to-tickets`). The Q/T boundary above is the gate between them — do not flatten the two into one queue.
- **"Phase", unqualified, is not board vocabulary.** It refers only to the [7-phases method](https://www.aihero.dev/my-7-phases-of-ai-development)'s numbered phases and appears only in the status line's method citation, always as "the method's phase N".

*Translation for the closed record* — plan-history.md, grill-history.md, the ADRs and commit messages are **not rewritten** (an ADR saying "ruled during Slice B" is a historical fact); read their retired vocabulary through this table:

| In the record | Read as |
|---|---|
| Milestones **M0–M6** | the walking skeleton's waypoints — all built, spec removed 2026-08-04, record in plan-history.md |
| **"Phase A / B / C"** (before 2026-08-04) | Waypoints A / B / C |
| **"Phase 1–7"**, "Phase 6", "Phase 7 QA" | the 7-phases method's stages; this board is its execution board and the QA pass raises tickets here |
| Slice Ask's **"Phase 0 / 1 / 2"** | that slice's own discovery / specification / gate-questions stages, all closed 2026-07-31 |
| **Waves 0–8**, **P1–P4** | slice-local sublabels, unchanged and still in use |

## ⚠ One named build-time decision — skeleton auth

The design layer defers real identity/security to the infra/security session (component 1, open). The skeleton still needs a login. **Decision taken for the skeleton, to be superseded by that session:** email + password session login for the seeded users (`POST /auth/session`, httpOnly cookie), plus Entra ID SSO on the Copilot path (M6, where Microsoft mandates it). No self-serve signup, no password reset, no roles beyond what the data model already carries. This is scaffolding, not the security model; it is listed here so it is a recorded choice, not an accident.

**Production identity is committed as Entra-first (recorded 2026-07-04):** most users will arrive through Microsoft Entra (Azure AD), so production login is Entra ID SSO (OIDC) as the primary path, with the skeleton's password login retained only as a break-glass/dev mechanism to be decided at the infra/security session. The build already enables this: identity is established at one API boundary only (T-021/T-023, contracts principle 3), `User.external_identity` carries the Entra subject from Drawer 1, and T-071 exercises the full Entra → User → Participant mapping. Adding web SSO later is an additive login route, not a rework.

## Building for V1

Every ticket in this part ships in the pilot, sequenced by [v1.md](v1.md)'s
waypoints, except where an entry carries an explicit **→ beyond V1** marker
(a handful of tickets minted inside otherwise-live slices before the V1 cut).
Work deferred from the destination lives in
[Beyond V1 — the deferred register](#beyond-v1--the-deferred-register), each
entry naming its gate and where its design lives.

**Slice Ask — The agent harness: Ask becomes a typed-worker, planned, evaluable analysis surface** — 🎯 **discovered + specified 2026-07-29 (the design folded into this board 2026-07-31); T-245–T-299 ticketed, Wave 0 part-built; MVP scoped to end at Lens 2026-07-31 (ruling below).** Ask today is a four-step coded chain behind a thin chat screen (T-052/T-088). This slice makes it an agent harness: seven typed workers, a persisted and editable **plan artefact**, two honestly-labelled orchestration modes, task-class model routing inside the existing ADR-0037 tier router, **Lens** personas as declarative domain content, scoping questions, Teach, and — landing early rather than last — an **eval harness** with mandatory permission cases on every build. **The Ask specification (the slice's own "Phase 1" document) was folded into this board on 2026-07-31 and its folder deleted** — the design content now sits in the wave reference blocks below and in the ticket entries themselves, the Lens definitions at [packages/lenses/definitions/](../../packages/lenses/definitions/), and the eval harness's own machinery at [evals/README.md](../../evals/README.md). Its discovery report ("Phase 0") was a dated snapshot of a codebase that has since moved; its live half is the findings table below.

*Owner rulings, the Ask gate questions (2026-07-29) — **recorded in the ADRs they amended, not restated here** (pointer-ised 2026-07-31, because a board holding its own copy of a ruling is how the two drift apart):* both orchestration modes ship, honestly labelled (**ADR-0027 §3**, **ADR-0028 §5**); web-research results are citable in a separate external register (**ADR-0022** amended; user-pinned attached sources unchanged); the persona is a **Lens**, not a role (**CONTEXT.md**); the consenting vocabulary is admitted to **CONTEXT.md**; ~~Teach carries no aggregation across customers (**ADR-0026** applied unchanged)~~ — **↩ reversed 2026-08-26** by the signals session, see [ADR-0026](../architecture/adr/0026-distillation-egress-boundary.md)'s amendment; the authority corpus is two-tier (**ADR-0023** extended); a citation must be checkable, not merely precise; and there is no user-facing orchestration-mode selector — the Tools chip already expresses that intent. Full reasoning for each: [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md).

*The eleven non-negotiables — folded 2026-07-31 from the Ask specification's index, and the constraint set every ticket in this slice answers to.* **Where a requirement and a non-negotiable conflict, the non-negotiable wins.** *(Six of the eleven were moved out to their component docs the same day — they are properties of the access model and the engine that outlive this slice, and four of them already hold in the running system. Only the pointer stays here; the board keeps the five that are genuinely about **unbuilt worker architecture**.)*

1. **No assertion without provenance.** Every factual claim resolves to a document, a version, and **either a locator or the verbatim passage** — the property that matters is that a reader can *check* it, and a citation nobody can check is functionally an uncited claim. Uncited claims are a build failure, not a style issue. *(True for the grounded register today. The locator-or-quote half was open at MVP and **closed 2026-08-04 by T-271** for any document ingested since: an assembled passage carries a character span, a derived paragraph, and the verbatim source text at that span. **Two residuals, stated rather than implied** — a chunk ingested *before* T-271 carries no span and degrades to version grain until re-ingested, and **page** remains unavailable until a PDF input path exists (T-305), which matters because page is the locator a planner actually names.)*
2–5. **The four enforcement invariants — permissions at the data layer never in a prompt; scope never escalates; label propagation; untrusted content never shares a context window with corpus content.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-2-access.md §7](../architecture/components/component-2-access.md).** They are properties of the *access component*, not of Ask, and four of them already hold in the running system with a guard keeping them true (T-247, T-249, T-250, ADR-0029). A property the code has belongs in the component doc; the board keeps only the pointer.
6. **Workers return structured data, not prose.** The chat agent sees a worker's output object, never its reasoning trace.
7. **Workers are leaves.** Only the chat agent orchestrates. The single exception is `workflow_runner`, which executes a pre-declared DAG.
8. **No generic escape-hatch worker.** No `research_agent`, no `code_execution`, no `do_the_thing`. An eighth worker is almost always a workflow that has not been declared yet.
9. **The system never gives an unqualified professional opinion.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-6-engine.md §6](../architecture/components/component-6-engine.md).** A product boundary on what the engine may say, not an Ask constraint.
10. **Document version status is respected everywhere.** Superseded documents are excluded by default and their use is always flagged. *(Exclusion true today; deliberate opt-in with flagging is T-273.)*
11. **A Lens changes register, never reach.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-6-engine.md §6](../architecture/components/component-6-engine.md)**, with the reach half owned by [component-2 §7](../architecture/components/component-2-access.md). Verified here by T-281's signature test and eval case `PERM-05`.

*Deliberately outside this slice:* **streaming** (additive and orthogonal); **cross-project and workspace-scoped Ask** (deferred by ADR-0031 §3 — one assembly environment per request stands); **a gold-standard case library** (the harness plus a seed set is the deliverable; authoring the real library is the domain expert's work); and **the org-built worker** (build-your-own, F — the registry is designed so one is expressible, but none is built).

*Scope ruling — **the MVP stops at Lens** (2026-07-31).* Owner-scoped: the skeleton/MVP needs Ask to return a **grounded, cited answer whose register changes with the Lens**, and nothing beyond that. The critical path is **Wave 4 — T-281 → T-299 → T-282 → T-283 — plus T-259**, and it depends on **none of Wave 2 or Wave 3**: a Lens is a prompt overlay on the existing coded chain, so the plan executor (T-261–T-268) and the worker registry (T-269–T-280) are post-MVP. Wave 4 needs **no migration** — `plans.lens_id` / `lens_version` already exist from 0035 and are written null pending T-299. Recommended *inside* the MVP despite being off the path: **T-251**, because a signed cookie cannot be revoked and that matters the moment this is in front of anyone. Deferred by this ruling: Wave 0's remainder (T-248, T-252, T-254, T-297), Waves 2 and 3, and Waves 5–8.

> **How this sits with V1 (reconciled 2026-07-31).** These are **two horizons, not two answers to one question.** The Ask MVP above is the near-term checkpoint — Ask returns a grounded, cited answer whose register changes with the Lens — and it is a **checkpoint inside [v1.md](v1.md)'s Waypoint B**, not a competing scope. V1 is the first pilot, and it needs the harness, the workers and the checker that this ruling defers. Nothing deferred here is deferred *out of V1*: T-254 (cost) and T-297 (RLS) sit in V1's **Waypoint A floor**, and Waves 2, 3, 5 and 8 sit in Waypoints B and C. Read the ruling as *what ships first*, never as *what V1 contains*. The sequence is **Ask MVP → V1 → beyond**.

**What the MVP therefore does not deliver, stated rather than discovered later:** three shared-core promises (the Wave 4 reference below) that the Lens files make and the runtime cannot yet keep — checkable provenance needs locators (~~T-270/T-271~~ ✅ **kept since 2026-08-04**, except page — T-305), staleness needs the authority corpus (T-276/T-277), absence detection needs `coverage_note` (T-272). The loader can refuse a Lens that *weakens* the core; it cannot make the runtime *keep* it. Non-negotiable 1 is therefore partly outstanding at MVP, and the Lens work does not close it.

*Wave 0 design reference — the eight findings, folded 2026-07-31 from the Ask discovery report and its remediation document.* An architecture interrogation of the running system, 2026-07-29, corrected 2026-07-30 once each finding was checked against what the code actually does. **Two were real leaks — F2 and F3 — and both describe material moving *within* one assembly environment, which is exactly what the environment cannot prevent.** Everything else is hardening, audit quality or cost. The severity ratings that did not survive scrutiny are recorded as struck, not deleted, because the reasoning is the useful part.

| # | Finding | Ticket | Blocks | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Conflict register — a person working for two clients | T-245/T-246 | nothing | ✅ **Downgraded.** Not a leak: a request runs in exactly one assembly environment (ADR-0025) and the gateway has no scope-widening parameter, so one client's material is unreachable from inside another's project whatever the person knows. An administrative guardrail at enrolment, never an input to `resolveAccess` |
| F2 | Label propagation on write-back | T-249 | the destination selector, `document_builder` | ✅ **A real leak.** Output took the writer's own organisation, not the most restrictive label among its sources |
| F3 | Untrusted content isolation | T-250 | `web_research` | ✅ **A real leak**, held by omission only — no web fetch path existed, and the prompt is built by concatenating `retrieved.items`, so any pipeline appending an item reached the model |
| F4 | Session lifetime and in-flight authority | T-251, T-252 | multi-worker plans | Open. Seconds today; minutes once a plan fans out |
| F5 | Passage-grain audit | T-253 | nothing | ✅ Converts "we log what it saw" from a claim into a demonstration |
| F6 | Defence in depth on the mandatory filter | T-247, T-297 | nothing | ✅ (chunks) / open (containers). Correct today *by construction*, and failing **open** at the database |
| F7 | Real cost attribution | T-254 | cost reporting | Open — every step in the live system records a cost of exactly zero; token counts are real |
| F8 | Scope attenuation | T-248 | nothing | **Downgraded.** Escalation is already structurally impossible; scope is *equal*, never narrowable, and equal scope leaks nothing because every worker runs inside the caller's single environment |

*Two requirements from that document that no ticket yet carries:* **revocation takes effect on the next plan step** (T-252's companion — consistent with the colocated store's immediate-effect property, ADR-0024, and live-mutable sandbox scope grants, ADR-0036); and **the rate-limit store moves off the per-process `Map`** ([rate-limit.ts:3](../../apps/api/src/rate-limit.ts#L3)) before multi-instance deployment — a named seam, restated under T-254 because one plan now means many model calls.

- **T-261 — Plan read API and permissions.** Producer-private, resolved through `resourceScope`; a different organisation gets the same 404 as nonexistence; edit-and-rerun restricted to the requesting Participant. The plan inherits the run's read scope *exactly* (the 2026-07-12 ruling): the run record is producer-private background data and the client reviews the **document** through the review cycle, never the agent's internals. **A colleague in the same organisation may read a plan but not re-run it as themselves** — re-running is a new Run with a new requester, which is the honest record. Also unblocks two things the eval harness records as absent by design: `expect_calls` (T-256) and the mode label (T-257). | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-262 — Execute from the plan.** The executor walks `plan.steps` honouring `depends_on`, replacing the hard-coded sequence. **The ground-check must stay outside the plan** — if it becomes a plan step a planner could skip it, which breaks the guarantee both modes rest on; asserted by a test. | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-263 — Step and run state migration.** `step_type` gains the worker step types; `run_state` gains `completed_with_failures`; a test asserts the contracts types and the DB enum cannot drift. | *(Deps: T-262)*
- **T-264 — Workflow DAG format, loader and validator.** `packages/workflows` is an empty stub today. Validation at load: every worker in the registry, acyclic, resolvable `depends_on`, **no step may declare a scope** (inherited and not expressible), `writes` declaring its label-propagation behaviour, drafts non-production only. Each rule gets a fixture that fails it. | *(Deps: T-263)*
- **T-265 — `workflow_runner` and the first declared workflow.** The existing four-step chain declared as a DAG, changing no behaviour. The one non-leaf worker; keeping it from becoming a general escape hatch is review discipline, not a test. | *(Deps: T-264, T-269)*
- **T-266 — Model-chosen orchestration and mode labelling.** Classification into four outcomes; the dispatch loop over the **entitled** worker set. **Ground-check runs on every answer in both modes**, asserted for a plan that does not declare it. Mode on the plan, the run, Teach submissions and the footer. Largest risk is classification quality — a weak classifier routes everything to model-chosen and the product quietly becomes the generic agent the design forbids, which is why the fall-through rate is a reported metric. | *(Deps: T-265)*
- **T-267 — Plan edit and re-run.** View the plan, edit a step's inputs, remove a step, or add one from the entitled worker set, then re-run. **Editing is bounded by entitlement** — the set offered is the assembled set, so a user cannot add a worker they are not entitled to — and **editing cannot widen scope**, because a step's scope derives from the run's `EntitledSlice` and is not an editable field. Supersession, not mutation. **An edited plan is `model_chosen` even if it started `declared`** — a hand-edited workflow is no longer the declared workflow, and the UI says so at the point of editing. | *(Deps: T-266)*
- **T-268 — Partial failure semantics.** The current chain fails hard, which is too blunt for a multi-worker plan — one failed web search should not discard a completed corpus search. Failed step → dependants skipped, independent branches continue, `completed_with_failures` when output survived. **The answer body reports what did not run**, not only the footer — absence detection applied to the system's own failures. | *(Deps: T-266)*

*Wave 3 design reference — the seven typed workers, folded 2026-07-31.* Each declares a name, purpose, model tier, input and output schema, permitted tools, scope expression, whether it writes, and cacheability. **Workers return structured objects, never prose** — the chat agent sees a worker's output object, never its reasoning trace, which keeps its context unpolluted and the audit record checkable rather than narrative. **Workers are leaves**; only the chat agent orchestrates, the single exception being `workflow_runner`. **There is no eighth worker and no generic one** — no `research_agent`, no `code_execution`, no `do_the_thing`. A capability that seems to want an eighth worker is almost certainly a workflow that has not been declared yet, which is the good outcome: a declared workflow is evaluable end to end and an improvised worker is not.

| Worker | Returns | Tools | Scope | Tier | Writes | Cacheable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `corpus_retrieval` | ranked passages + coverage note | project indexes, doc store read | user ∩ project ∩ visibility | triage | no | yes |
| `authority_lookup` | provisions with version, in-force date + tier | authority index | standard tier (global) ∪ own org tier (org-private) | triage | no | yes |
| `web_research` | external sources, labelled untrusted | web search, fetch | **no corpus access** | mid | no | yes |
| `extractor` | schema-conforming records + failures | doc store read | inherits | mid, structured | no | yes |
| `workflow_runner` | the workflow's declared output | leaf workers per its DAG | inherits, cannot widen | per step | per declaration | no |
| `document_builder` | draft + source manifest + label | template store, doc store write | user ∩ project ∩ visibility, write | frontier | yes | no |
| `verifier` | per-claim verdict with locator | doc store read | inherits | frontier, other family | no | no |

*Two names were reconciled against CONTEXT.md, the vocabulary authority:* the brief's `canon_lookup` is **`authority_lookup`** (the canon is already the authority corpus, ADR-0023 — do not mint a second name for one thing) and its `matter` is **project** (matter is legal-sector vocabulary). **`authority_lookup` stays separate from `corpus_retrieval`:** the authority corpus is global, cacheable across every organisation, versioned by in-force date rather than document revision, and carries a different security posture. Different index, different freshness logic, different scope expression — **do not merge them.**

**Entitlement — the tool set is assembled, not filtered (T-269).** Only workers the user is entitled to enter the orchestrator's tool set: an unentitled worker is **absent, not disabled**, and the model is never told it exists — the same principle as the API's "denial and nonexistence read identically". Computed per request from three inputs: the requester's `EntitledSlice` (no slice, no workers at all); the deployment tier (a sovereign-tier deployment has no `web_research` because it admits no third-party egress — this falls out of the existing router policy rather than needing a new switch); and the organisation's own authority shelf. **Every user therefore gets a materially different agent** — different Lens overlay, different worker set — assembled per request, not one agent with a filter bolted on.

**Audit shape.** A worker invocation is a **Step** in the existing append-only tree and in most cases a child **Run** — `parent_run_id` / `parent_step_id` / `child_run_id` already support this and the retrieve leaf already does exactly this. The only migration required is `step_type` gaining the worker step types (T-263); model id, usage, cost, egress facts, source set and rail outcomes are already on the Step row.

*Wave 3 — workers (T-269–T-280).* Two spikes start immediately and block nothing in Wave 0.
- **T-269 — Worker registry, typed contract, entitlement assembly.** ⭐ The declaration type plus one worker (`corpus_retrieval`). **The tool set is assembled from entitlements, not filtered** — an unentitled worker is absent, not disabled, and the model is never told it exists. A sovereign-tier deployment assembles no `web_research`, falling out of the existing router policy. | *(Deps: T-248, T-263)*
- ~~**T-270 — SPIKE: locator extraction.**~~ ✅ **Findings 2026-08-01**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- ~~**T-271 — Locators through the ingest pipeline.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-04** (migration 0039). Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- **T-272 — `corpus_retrieval`: coverage note, chunk ids, structured output.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `classification_terms?` (the ADR-0045 ontology pre-filter), `doc_types?`, `include_superseded=false`, `max_passages=20`. *Outputs:* `passages[]` — chunk_id, version_id, document_reference, document_title, version_reference, `superseded`, locator {page?, para?, section?}, text, relevance — plus `coverage_note`. **Substrate exists:** this is `groundedLibrary` reached through the assembly gateway, which already applies project, in-library, live-state, current-version, pinned-model and deliverable-visibility as SQL pre-filters in one query. The worker adds structure around it, **not a new path to the store**. The `coverage_note` states what corpus slice was searched, how many candidates the pre-filter admitted, and which requested terms found nothing — the mechanism behind absence detection. **The cache key is `query + corpus_version + scope_hash`**, where `corpus_version` must change when any admitted document changes and `scope_hash` is computed from the resolved `EntitledSlice`, never from the request; a cache without scope in the key is a permission bypass with extra steps. | *(Deps: T-269, T-253)*
- **T-273 — `include_superseded` with mandatory flagging.** Default exclusion unchanged. A superseded source carries a flag **in the prose at the point of use**, not only in the manifest — easy to render in the footer and easy to forget where it matters. | *(Deps: T-272)*
- **T-274 — `extractor` and the named schemas.** *Inputs:* `schema_name` (commitments | consultee_responses | mitigation_measures | exa_questions | deadlines | parameters), `scope` as `{version_ids}` or `{query}`, `strict=true`. *Outputs:* `records[]` each with source + locator, `failures[]` (reason, source, locator, partial_record), `extraction_note`. Structured output only — no narrative. The named schemas are **versioned domain content beside the Lens files**, owned by the same specialists: adding a schema is a content change and the extractor's code does not change. `strict` defaults true and `failures` is a first-class output — **a silently coerced commitment is worse than no record**, because the whole value of a commitments register is that it is complete and checkable; failures feed absence detection. Non-negotiable 1 applies to structured output exactly as to prose: **every record carries source and locator**. | *(Deps: T-269)*
- **T-275 — `verifier` on an independent model family.** ⛅ **→ beyond V1** (v1.md stubs the verifier; the deterministic ground-check carries the guarantee). *Inputs:* `claims[{text, source_ref}]`, `sources[{version_id, locator, text}]`. *Outputs:* `verdicts[]` — claim_text, `supported | partial | unsupported | contradicted`, source_ref, locator, rationale — plus a count summary. Per-claim verdicts **on top of** the deterministic ground-check, never instead of it — asserted by a test that removes the verifier from a plan and finds ground-check still ran. **The distinction is easy to lose and is the point:** the deterministic check asks *does this claim resolve to a source the run actually saw* (pure code, provable, every answer, both modes, always) and the verifier asks *does that source actually **support** the claim* (frontier model, probabilistic, only when the plan declares it). The floor is the deterministic check; the verifier catches what the floor cannot see — a real citation attached to a claim it does not support. Deleting the floor to "replace it with the verifier" would be a straight downgrade of the system's central claim. Where no independent family conforms to the tier, verification is **unavailable and skipped with a stated reason**, never silently same-family. | *(Deps: T-269, T-286)*
- ~~**T-276 — SPIKE: the authority corpus.**~~ ✅ **Findings 2026-08-27**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- **T-277 — Authority corpus store and ingest.** ⛅ **→ beyond V1** (the authority corpus is out of V1, both tiers; only the T-276 spike is frontier work). 🔒 **Two tiers, owner-ruled 2026-07-29 (ADR-0023 extended).** *Standard* — Infora-shipped and universal (Planning Act 2008, EIA and Habitats Regulations, NPSs, PINS Advice Notes, s.51 advice, precedent DCOs and Decision Letters), deliberately confined to material Infora can ship freely under Crown copyright / OGL, **which is why Infora buys no per-customer standards subscriptions**. *Organisation* — added by the organisation's owner (licensed ISO/BSI standards, sector guidance, its own policy instruments), held in that organisation's portable org context (ADR-0020) and never crossing the wall. **Two organisations on one project can hold different shelves and therefore legitimately return different answers to the same question** — correct, and surfaced by the `tier` field on every provision rather than hidden. **Why an org-tier provision still grounds and cites** despite living in org context, which ADR-0020 says informs only: ADR-0021 already fixed that surface placement does not set channel role. What matters is what the material *is* — a firm's own precedent and know-how informs and is never cited, because its provenance is entangled with clients' (ADR-0026 Filters 1–2); a published external instrument with an issuing body, a version and an in-force date grounds and is cited, because none of that is true of it. Both tiers. A query for a past `in_force_at` returns the version in force **at that date**. **An organisation's tier is invisible to every other organisation** — a wall test, not merely a scoping one. Org-tier entries cannot be recorded as Infora-maintained. | *(Deps: T-276)*
- **T-278 — `authority_lookup`.** ⛅ **→ beyond V1** (rides the authority corpus, out of V1). 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `instrument_types?` (act | regulations | nps | advice_note | s51_advice | decision_letter | standard | guidance | policy), `in_force_at?` defaulting to today. *Outputs:* `provisions[]` — authority_ref, instrument_title, instrument_version, `tier: standard | organisation`, in_force_from/to, superseded_by, `currency: infora_maintained | org_declared`, last_reviewed (org tier only), locator, text, relevance — plus `currency_note`. **`in_force_at` is the load-bearing input:** consenting questions are frequently about the position *at a past date* (which NPS applied at acceptance, which Advice Note version the ES was drafted against), and versioning by in-force date rather than document revision is precisely why this cannot be `corpus_retrieval` with a flag. **`currency_note` reports per tier because the two guarantees are not equal** — Infora operates currency for the standard tier and cannot know a customer's uploaded standard has been superseded, so an org-tier entry says "org-declared, last reviewed <date>" rather than implying Infora's guarantee. Standard tier ∪ the requester's own organisation tier, cache keyed on `org_shelf_version` — a cache keyed only on the query would serve one firm's private shelf to another. | *(Deps: T-277, T-269)*
- **T-279 — `web_research`.** ⛅ **→ beyond V1** (external dependency, stubbed by v1.md). 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `recency?` (any | past_year | past_month), `max_sources=8`. *Outputs:* `sources[]` — url, publisher, title, published_date, retrieved_at, excerpt, relevance, and `trust: 'external-untrusted'` as a **constant, not computed** — plus `search_note`. Cache key `query + recency + day-bucket`. **The whole safety case is that a prompt injection in a fetched page cannot reach client data, because the worker holding the injected text never holds corpus data.** In `packages/external` behind the T-250 barrier: no `Db`, no `assemble`, no `EntitledSlice`, proven by the dep rule. **The orchestrator is the only place the two meet, and it meets them as data, not as a shared context window.** A `web.fetch` is egress and is recorded on the Step alongside model egress (ADR-0037 §6); a sovereign-tier deployment has this worker absent entirely, via T-269's entitlement rather than a switch. Corpus content never present in its context, asserted by inspecting its actual inputs. User-pinned web attached sources remain non-citing — the two halves of the ADR-0022 amendment. | *(Deps: T-250, T-269)*
- **T-280 — `document_builder`.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `template_id`, `brief`, `sources: {version_ids}` — **explicit, never "whatever you find"**, because the builder does not retrieve; the orchestrator hands it ids it got from `corpus_retrieval`, which keeps label computation tractable and the manifest honest — and `destination`. *Outputs:* `document_id`, `manifest[]` (version_id, document_reference, version_reference, locator, used_for), `label {computed_label, most_restrictive_input, destination_label}`, `withheld[]`. **Partly exists:** the chain's `document` mode already drafts into a sandbox document via suggestions, grounded-only, with unsourced claims withheld; new are the template, the manifest and the label. The `label` output is not decoration — it is the evidence that propagation happened. Draft into a template with a source manifest and the computed label enforced against the destination. `sources` is explicit — the builder does not retrieve, which keeps the label computation tractable and the manifest honest. | *(Deps: T-249, T-269)*

*Wave 4 design reference — the Lens, folded 2026-07-31.* **A Lens is how an answer reads, never what a user can reach.** Ask serves several kinds of professional off one corpus: a planning specialist and a communications lead asking the same question about the same noise assessment need different register, depth, ordering and follow-ups. They do **not** need different data, and giving them different data would be a security control hiding inside a preference. Same corpus, same workers, same permissions — different Lens. *Naming:* "role" is taken (Membership role, ADR-0015/0016), so the persona is a **Lens** (CONTEXT.md) and **nothing here may be implemented as a `role` field.**

**The shared core — every Lens inherits these, and a Lens file cannot override, weaken or opt out of any of them:** (1.1) **provenance** — no claim without a citation to document, version and *either a locator or the verbatim passage*, because the property protected is checkability, and a version-level citation on a 200-page chapter is one nobody opens; (1.2) **three registers always distinguished** — Record (what the document says, quoted or closely paraphrased), Inference (what Ask concludes, explicitly flagged, with the record it rests on cited), Authority (what the canon provides, cited to instrument and in-force version), plus the ADR-0022 amendment's fourth, External (badged untrusted-external: URL, publisher, date, retrieval timestamp), which never renders like the other three; (1.3) **no unqualified professional opinion** — never that a scheme will secure consent, that an assessment is compliant, or that a position is legally sound; it presents the test, the evidence before it, and the precedent; (1.4) **staleness** — an answer resting on a revised instrument says so and names the version relied on; (1.5) **absence detection** — actively report what is *missing*: the unaddressed chapter, the open commitment, the consultee who never responded, the ExA question that was not answered; (1.6) **honest uncertainty** — not every sentence hedged into mush, not a weak inference dressed as a finding; (1.7) **version discipline** — never rely on a superseded document without flagging it *at the point of use*, not in a footnote.

**The overlay schema** (the authoritative files are [packages/lenses/definitions/](../../packages/lenses/definitions/), with its authoring guide): `id` (kebab-case, never reused), `label`, `description`, `status: active | draft`, `version` (bumped on any change, recorded per request); `register: {jargon: peer|explained|avoided, acronyms: unexpanded|first-use-expanded|avoided, reading_level}`; `default_depth`, `answer_shape[]` (ordered — what leads, what follows), `default_output: prose|table|bullet-brief|draft-text|qa-pairs`, `citation_display: inline|footnote|appendix`; `clarifying_bias[]`, `escalation_language[]`, `preferred_workers[]`, `prohibitions[]`; `example_exchanges[]` (2–3 worked pairs, used as eval cases). **What each field may not do:** `preferred_workers` is a **ranking hint for the planner, not an entitlement** — a Lens naming a worker the user is not entitled to changes nothing, because the tool set is assembled from entitlements first; `prohibitions` are **additive to the shared core, never subtractive**; `answer_shape` cannot introduce a section with no data behind it (an empty section is omitted, not filled); `escalation_language` supplies phrasing for risk and never changes *whether* a risk is reported.

| id | Register | Leads with | Escalation is | The load-bearing prohibition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planning-environmental` | peer, full jargon, acronyms unexpanded | the statutory or policy test, and whether the evidence meets it | examination risk | never predict an examination outcome; never conflate PEIR with ES; never treat a REAC commitment as discretionary |
| `engineer` | peer, design vocabulary | the physical or design implication and the constraint it creates | constraint on the design envelope, incl. Rochdale parameter conflicts | never offer planning-law interpretation; never present a consented commitment as an option |
| `project-manager` | programme and delivery, tabular | what is due, who owns it, what is at risk and by when | programme ("this sits on the critical path to Deadline 3") | **never state a date not in the corpus or canon, and never present an inferred deadline as fixed** — inferred dates carry a visible marker |
| `communications` | plain English, acronyms expanded or avoided | what it means for people, and what may be said publicly | reputational and consistency risk | **distinguishes published from unpublished and prominently flags anything not yet public**; never soften a formal commitment; never generate a quotation attributed to a named person |
| `commercial` *(draft)* | — | — | — | ships incomplete **on purpose**, to prove the extension path and to fail validation informatively if promoted to `active` as-is |

**Extension without a code change (T-281).** All files in one directory, read and validated at startup; the set is immutable for the process lifetime in production and hot-reloaded in non-production, so a domain expert editing a file sees the effect without a restart. **Validation failures are build failures, not degradations:** unknown field, missing required field, value outside an enum, a `prohibitions` entry attempting to negate a shared-core rule, a duplicate or retired `id`, `preferred_workers` naming a worker not in the registry *(deferred — see T-281)*, or `status: active` with empty `example_exchanges`. **Failure messages name the file, the field and the rule in language a domain expert can act on** — not a schema-library stack trace. That is a stated acceptance criterion, because error-message quality is where an "engineers only" system quietly reasserts itself.

*Wave 4 — Lens (T-281, T-299, T-282, T-283).* **The MVP's terminal wave** (scope ruling above). Prompt-and-surface only; independently shippable; **no migration** — 0035 already carries `plans.lens_id` / `lens_version`. **T-281 built 2026-08-01** (no migration; lenses 50/50, full check green).
- ~~**T-281 — `packages/lenses`: loader, validator, one Lens wired.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-01**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- ~~**T-299 — The Lens through the request and into the prompt.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-01**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- ~~**T-282 — The four active Lenses and the draft.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-01**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- ~~**T-283 — Lens switching, persistence, logging.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-01**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#slice-ask).

- **T-284 — Task-class routing.** `Router.chat(task, …)` accepts a task argument and currently ignores it — the seam exists, the routing does not. **Tier conformance applies before task selection**, unchanged; the ordering is easy to invert when adding the second axis. | *(Deps: T-263)*
- **T-285 — Fallback chains.** Per tier, documented, for provider outage or rate limiting. A fallback is attempted only if it also conforms to the deployment tier; **availability is never traded for conformance** — already the router's behaviour, and adding fallbacks must not weaken it. An exhausted chain fails the step with a stated reason and the run continues per T-268. Every attempt, including failures, writes a Step audit row with egress facts, so a fallback that fired is visible in the record. | *(Deps: T-284)*
- **T-286 — The verify independence constraint.** ⛅ **→ beyond V1** (rides the verifier, stubbed by v1.md). Enforced in code at dispatch, not left to whoever edits the config: the router resolves the family that produced the claims **from the plan's draft step** and refuses to dispatch verification to it. **Where every conforming route belongs to one family, verification is *unavailable* and the plan step is `skipped` with a stated reason — never silently run same-family**, which matters most at the sovereign tier where self-hosted open-weight models may be the only conforming routes. Skipped verification is visible in the completion footer and counted in the eval report: a run that could not be independently verified says so. Also the point at which the eval harness's own grader stops using the harness-declared family (T-257) and reads the producing family from the run. | *(Deps: T-284)*

*Wave 8 design reference — the Ask interface, folded 2026-07-31.* Layout: a progress rail on the left, the transcript centre with a completion footer under each answer, the existing source panel on the right (T-105, unchanged), and the composer carrying five chips.

**Composer chips.** *Lens* — shows the active label, and the picker states **in the picker itself, not in a tooltip**: *"A Lens changes how answers are written. It does not change what you can see."* Draft Lenses never appear in production; changing it re-renders the **next** answer and history keeps the Lens it was produced under. *Model* — shows the router's choice with an **Auto** indicator ("Auto · Opus"); a pin is **per-conversation, never sticky**, is logged on the plan and shown in cost reporting, and **the tier constraint is not overridable** — a non-conforming model is *absent from the list, not disabled*. *Data sources* — how many are in scope, with a **warning state when none**, because a grounded answer over an empty scope is the single most misleading state Ask can be in; the list is built from the same `deliverableVisibleSql` pre-filter as retrieval, **so the chip cannot show a document the answer could not have used**, and refinement **narrows, never widens** (intersected server-side — a relevance control, not an access one). *Tools* — browse and pin codified workflows; "Tools" not "Skills" (CONTEXT.md, T-109), and pinning **biases** classification toward a workflow without forcing it, which is the reason there is no user-facing mode selector. *Context indicator* — budget consumed against the assembly budget, informational. Teach sits on completed responses, not in the composer.

**Output destination selector** (T-295) — at the top of a new conversation. **This carries permission consequences and is not a preference.** Destinations are the sandboxes the user can reach at their real scope; **warn visibly when the destination is broader than the source material**, naming both labels — *"This answer draws on material restricted to 3 named people. The selected destination is shared with 2 organisations."*; **broader than sources blocks by default**, with an explicit override recorded on the plan and in the audit trail, while narrower is allowed without a warning. **It cannot ship before F2 is closed** — a destination selector without label propagation is a UI implying a guarantee the backend does not make.

**The progress rail** (T-293) — the stage vocabulary rendered in the user's words: *Understanding your question · Loading context · Scoping · Searching project documents · Checking the consenting canon · Researching publicly available sources · Planning the analysis · Running the analysis · Verifying citations · Report.* All four rules are load-bearing: a stage that did not run is **never shown as having run**; a conditional stage that was not needed is absent or shown explicitly as not run, never quietly completed; failed and skipped stages show as failed and skipped; and transitions come from the plan's step states, **never a client-side timer** — a rail driven by a timer is a lie that happens to look right most of the time.

**The completion footer** (T-294) — always visible: what was produced in one line; **the orchestration mode in words** (*"Ran the declared workflow: Answer a question about the project"* / *"Composed for this question"*), a hard requirement rather than a nicety; the Lens and version; counts of claims cited, withheld and labelled open-world, read off the existing `railOutcomes`; and **where verification could not be taken independently, say so**. Behind a Details affordance: the plan artefact rendered as steps with their states, editable and re-runnable; the workers invoked; per-step model and cost with pinned models marked; and the full citation manifest — every source with document reference, version, locator and register.

**Rendering the four registers** (T-296) — *Record*: inline citation chip opening the source panel, carrying the **verbatim passage** where the source yields no reliable locator, never a bare version reference. *Inference*: visibly marked as inference, with the record it rests on cited. *Authority*: the instrument and its in-force version. *External*: **visually distinct from all three** — URL, publisher, date, retrieval timestamp, badged untrusted-external. **Different chip shape and colour, not a different tooltip:** a reader skim-reading must tell a web source from a project document without hovering. Superseded sources, where deliberately included, carry a flag **at the point of use in the prose**, not only in the manifest.

*Not in scope for this wave:* streaming (additive and orthogonal — the rail and footer are designed to accommodate it without rework, and the rail is its natural home); the Copilot surface (ADR-0031 makes it read-only with a bound project and no clarification round); and plan-editing beyond step inputs (reordering and branching are deferred — the artefact supports them, the surface starts with edit-and-rerun).

*Wave 8 — interface (T-292–T-296).*
- **T-292 — Composer chips.** Lens, Model, Data sources, Tools, Context. The Lens picker states in the picker that a Lens does not change what you can see. The Model chip lists only tier-conforming routes. **The Data sources chip warns when zero sources are in scope**, and refinement narrows only, intersected server-side. | *(Deps: T-283, T-284)*
- **T-293 — The progress rail.** Driven by plan step states, **never a client-side timer** — a timer-driven rail looks right most of the time, which is what makes it a trust problem rather than a bug. A stage that did not run is never shown as having run. | *(Deps: T-268)*
- **T-294 — The completion footer and plan view.** The orchestration mode stated **in words**, always visible; the Lens and version; Details exposing the plan, workers, per-step cost with pins marked, and the citation manifest. | *(Deps: T-267, T-293)*
- **T-295 — The output destination selector.** 🔒 A destination broader than the source material warns naming both labels and is blocked by default. Cannot ship before T-249 — a selector without propagation implies a guarantee the backend does not make. | *(Deps: T-249, T-280)*
- **T-296 — Four-register rendering.** Record, Inference, Authority and External **visually distinct by chip shape and colour, not by tooltip**. A reader skim-reading must tell a web source from a project document without hovering — the visible half of the ADR-0022 carve-out, and the half a client will judge. ⚠ **V1 ships the two-register degradation** ([v1.md](v1.md)'s named deviation): Authority (T-278) and External (T-279) are → beyond V1, so only Record and Inference render in the pilot; the four-register cut ships when those two return. | *(Deps: T-279, T-278, T-271)*

A refactor with its own risk profile; wants the same per-request seam as Wave 2. | *(Deps: T-247)*

*Waypoint C — the product surface (T-308–T-311).* ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-01 → [ADR-0048](../architecture/adr/0048-the-checker-findings-not-prose.md).** These four were ticketed hours earlier with three of them gated on `Q-007` (the rulebook's channel) and `Q-008` (the checker's output shape); both were ruled the same day, **as one decision rather than two**, and the entries below carry what the ruling changed. The remaining dependencies are ordinary ones — **T-328**, `extractor` (T-274) and locators (T-271) — not gates.
- ~~**T-308 — The rulebook's home.**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27** (migration 0051; unblocked 2026-08-01 by ADR-0048). Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#waypoint-c--the-product-surface).

- **T-309 — The document-creation DAG.** Largely composition, and the unblocked half of Waypoint C: `document_builder` (T-280) wrapped in a declared workflow — drafting into a template with an explicit source manifest and the computed label enforced against the destination. No new capability; the value is that a declared workflow is **evaluable end to end** where an improvised one is not. | *(Deps: T-264, T-265, T-280)*
- **T-310 — The checker DAG.** ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-01 → ADR-0048.** The new capability, and the one a consultancy will judge: the agent reviews a draft against three inputs — the **corpus** (grounded, cites normally), **manually attached documents** (ADR-0022 — never grounds, never cited), and the firm's **rulebook** (quoted verbatim, never cited) — and returns **structured, anchored findings rather than prose**. Three inputs, three honest treatments, one schema. **It checks; it does not write** — a finding's optional proposed revision enters the existing accept/edit/reject Suggestion path and is never auto-applied, so the checker gains no write path the drafting side lacks. **A finding states a defect, never a verdict** (component 6 §6's first answer invariant). ⚠ **This ticket builds the capability, not a way to reach it** — how a declared workflow is launched is `Q-030`, raised 2026-08-01 and unruled. Do not invent an invocation path here — that is `Q-030`, and its answer arrives as a separate ticket. | *(Deps: T-328, T-274, T-271, T-308)*
- **T-311 — The marked-up edit: the checker's output surface.** ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-01 → ADR-0048**, which decided the surface rather than following it; **re-scoped the same day on the owner's steer** from "a findings list" to **a marked-up edit the reviewer accepts or rejects change by change**, which is also how the Word add-in (B) already behaves (tracked changes carrying citation and rationale). **The finding stays the unit; the mark is its rendering** — each mark is hoverable to the rule it enforces and the evidence behind it, so a mark is explicable rather than a mystery diff. **Anchoring is the whole point**: a mark that does not sit in the text is a report, not a tool. **Two obligations are load-bearing and easy to miss:** a **quoted rule must render differently from a grounded citation** (it is not a source chip and must not resolve like one), or ADR-0048's distinction survives in the model and dies on the screen; and a **quoted rule is org-private**, so a mark quoting Org B's manual must never appear on a surface Org A reads — an ethical-wall breach delivered by a feature nobody thinks of as crossing the wall. **Per-mark resolution, no bulk-accept** (ADR-0048 §3). ⚠ **Caveat, not a dependency:** `Q-031` asks whether that guard survives at fifty marks. Build the per-mark surface; if `Q-031` rules a middle, it arrives as its own ticket rather than reopening this one. | *(Deps: T-328, T-310)*
- ~~**T-328 — The finding schema.**~~ ✅ **Built**. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md#waypoint-c--the-product-surface).

- **T-313 — Attribute the cost of embedding.** T-254 priced the chat calls; **`EmbedResult` carries no token usage at all**, so the retrieval half of every run's cost is invisible and no rate table can price it. The adapter must report usage before anything else is possible — this is a `packages/model` change first and an attribution change second. Until it lands, a run's recorded cost is the **drafting** cost and the report should not imply otherwise. | *(Deps: T-254)*
- **T-314 — The rate-limit store moves off the per-process `Map`.** Named as a seam at T-217 and restated by the Wave 0 reference under T-254, because **one plan now means many model calls**. [rate-limit.ts:3](../../apps/api/src/rate-limit.ts#L3) is an in-process sliding window: correct on one instance, and silently N× the intended limit on N. It is a throttle protecting credential guessing and paid model calls, so the failure is quiet and expensive rather than visible. **Unblocked 2026-08-01 — the store is Postgres, not Redis.** The infra session ruled against standing up ElastiCache for this: the database is already there, and at ≤ 200 runs/day plus login attempts the throughput is trivial, so a cache tier would be infrastructure bought for its own sake. Revisit if [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md)'s trigger 3 fires. | *(Deps: T-316)*

**Slice V1-I — The pilot deployment** *(ruled 2026-08-01, the infra/security decision session → [ADR-0047](../architecture/adr/0047-pilot-deployment-substrate.md), amending ADR-0037. T-316–T-327.)* The gate [v1.md](v1.md) names: everything above runs on a `docker compose` Postgres with no object store, and **no external pilot begins until this slice does**. The session decided; this is the build. Sequence T-316 first — six of the eleven that follow depend on it.

- **T-316 — The pilot environment as Terraform.** One AWS account in `eu-west-2`: VPC across two AZs (an RDS subnet group and an ALB both require it, so this is not redundancy theatre), ALB with **AWS WAF managed rules**, ECS Fargate, **RDS PostgreSQL 17 single-AZ with managed PITR** at five-minute granularity and 14-day retention, S3 for both the file store and the web build, CloudFront + ACM, ECR, **customer-managed KMS keys** for S3/RDS/Secrets Manager with annual rotation, Secrets Manager, and the IAM roles. RDS is **not publicly accessible** and admits 5432 only from the task security group; S3 is reached over a **gateway endpoint** so object traffic never touches NAT. Lives in `infra/`, **outside the pnpm workspace** — keeping it out leaves `scripts/dep-rules.mjs` and the package graph untouched, which is the reason to prefer Terraform over CDK here. State in S3 with DynamoDB locking. **The environment must be recreatable from source, or T-325 is meaningless.** | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-317 — S3 behind `file_ref`, and the API always serves the bytes.** ADR-0043 §1 anticipated this: `file_ref` was "a pointer either way", and today there is no object store behind it at all. Bucket private with Block Public Access and versioning on, SSE-KMS, object keys namespaced by organisation and project so an object's tenancy is legible from the key alone. **No presigned URLs — this is the load-bearing constraint, not a preference.** A presigned URL is a bearer capability that outlives the entitlement check that minted it, so the wall would hold at the API and leak at the object store, directly contradicting ADR-0024's revoke-in-the-same-transaction guarantee and ADR-0036's grants. The API re-resolves entitlement and streams on every read; ADR-0043's WOPI host has to serve `GetFile`/`PutFile` itself regardless, so this falls out rather than costing extra. | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-318 — The deployment pipeline, migrate-then-deploy.** GitHub Actions with **OIDC federation to an IAM role — no long-lived AWS keys are minted for CI or for a human**. On merge to `main`: `pnpm run check` (unchanged — CI's fast half; CI adds the audit, migrate, seed, eval smoke, build and e2e) → build and push images to ECR → **run migrations as a one-off ECS task using the owner credential** → deploy the API service revision → smoke `/health` → sync the web build to S3 and invalidate CloudFront. The separate migration task is the point: it preserves the T-247 two-role split through the pipeline instead of only in development, so the running application never holds a credential that can alter schema. **Two environments only — local `docker compose` and `pilot`; there is no staging**, deliberately, revisited at [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md)'s trigger 2. | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-319 — The `pilot` deployment tier.** A `TIER_POLICIES` entry and one more value in the `env.ts` enum — a policy addition exactly as ADR-0037 §2 promised, touching no structure. Attributes are declared **true**: `region: us`, `retention: zero`, `jurisdiction: foreign-reachable`, `eligibility: enterprise-zdr`, `classifications: ['official']`. Tests must assert the three properties that stop it becoming a back door: it is **never the default** (`standard` stays the default), it is the **only tier admitting `us`**, and a request classified above OFFICIAL **fails closed** against it. ⚠ **Build it now; it must not be *used* until the zero-data-retention agreement with Anthropic is in place** — absent that, `retention: zero` is a lie told to our own router, which is worse than having no router. **Owner-ruled 2026-08-01: obtaining the agreement is the *last* step, so this ticket ends at built-and-tested and the cutover is T-333.** | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-320 — A second chat adapter (Bedrock), because one implementation is an assertion.** The owner's requirement is that switching provider be configuration, not a rebuild — and an interface with a single implementation cannot demonstrate that. Build the Bedrock chat adapter with route attributes supplied by configuration, and test that a configuration change switches the route and that each tier still fails closed when nothing conforms. The value is the proof, not the adapter. 🔗 **Two-for-one, if you point it at the right family (raised 2026-08-01).** T-282 ruled the eval grader as human review, with a revisit trigger that **fired** when ADR-0047 named a second provider — but a second *provider* is not a second *family*, and Bedrock-served Claude is the family the build already runs on, so grading Claude with Claude is not independence. **If this adapter is pointed at a non-Anthropic family on Bedrock (Llama, Mistral, Nova, Cohere) rather than at Claude, it also unblocks the eleven `ungraded` eval cases** — the same work, one deliberate choice of model id. See `evals/README.md`, "The grader ruling for the MVP". | *(Deps: T-319)*
- **T-321 — A second embedding adapter, and the deliberate re-index.** 🔺 **Sequencing dependency, not just a portability proof (raised 2026-08-01).** The router checks conformance on the **embedding** route too, and embeddings run on the **ingest path** — so while embeddings sit on a US vendor with no retention agreement, **the corpus cannot be loaded into the pilot environment at all**. Moving them to Bedrock puts them under the AWS agreement, which needs no separate negotiation, and leaves only *generation* waiting on Anthropic. **Do this before the corpus load, not after.** Same argument as T-320 otherwise, plus the ADR-0024 consequence: embeddings are pinned per index, so a provider switch **forces a deliberate re-index rather than a silent mix** — and the ingest path must refuse a mismatched index rather than blend it. At 100–500 documents the re-index is minutes, which is precisely why proving this now is cheap and proving it at a hundred thousand documents would not be. | *(Deps: T-320)*
- **T-322 — Pilot user provisioning, and the shared dev password out of the pilot.** The owner ruled 2026-08-01 that **password authentication carries V1** and Entra follows (ADR-0047 §14). This ticket is the condition that makes the deferral defensible rather than merely accepted: seed data is development-only, and **pilot users are provisioned individually** — the seeded shared `wrenfield-dev` password must not exist in the pilot environment. Add a provisioning path and a startup check that refuses to boot the `pilot` tier against seeded credentials. **This is the single largest risk in the identity deferral, and it is a build task, not a note.** | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-323 — Amazon SES as the notification transport.** The provider ruled (ADR-0047 §16): SES in `eu-west-2` — in-region, IAM-native, no additional vendor or DPA. This ticket builds the **transport seam and the domain/DKIM setup only**; *what* gets sent, and when, is `Q-012` and is designed separately. Two lead-time items ride outside the board: DKIM domain verification, and **SES starts in sandbox mode**, able to send only to verified addresses until production access is approved. | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-324 — Error tracking: Sentry, EU region, PII scrubbing on.** [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md) requires error tracking before the pilot and console-only is not a pilot posture. Sentry's non-US option is an EU region, not a UK one, so this is **the third part of the three-part residency statement** and must be configured to carry telemetry and stack traces only — **no document content, no prompt or completion bodies**. | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-325 — Rehearse the restore, and write it up.** [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md) commits to RPO ≤ 1 hour and RTO ≤ 8 business hours, and both are claims until exercised. Restore RDS to a point in time and recover S3 objects **into a scratch environment**, time it against the RTO line, and write up what happened. **An untested backup is not a backup**, and a live pilot carrying a real firm's documents is the wrong place to discover that. | *(Deps: T-316, T-318)*
- **T-326 — The Collabora dev-harness in `docker compose`.** ADR-0043 §3's engine target, settled 2026-08-01: **Collabora Online Development Edition**, chosen over OnlyOffice because OnlyOffice's primary integration is its own Document Server API with WOPI secondary, so Collabora exercises the more representative WOPI surface — and the harness exists only to prove the WOPI host contract before pointing at real Office. **Local only; it is never deployed to the pilot environment**, since A3 P2 is build-and-validate and A3 P3 is gated on CSPP, outside V1. It therefore costs nothing to run. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-327 — The operability floor before the first external login.** `/health` wired into an uptime check, and structured request logs (T-219) retained ≥ 30 days in CloudWatch. Small, and [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md) makes it a precondition rather than a nicety — the pilot is the first time nobody is watching the terminal. | *(Deps: T-316, T-318)*
- **T-333 — The pilot-tier cutover.** The **last step before an external user logs in**, and a ticket rather than an assumption because it is the one action that turns a built system into a live one. Set `DEPLOYMENT_TIER=pilot`, attach the Anthropic route's real declared attributes, and **verify from the Step audit that recorded egress facts match the agreement** — the point of ADR-0037 §6 is that the posture is provable per call, so prove it once deliberately before trusting it. 🔒 **Blocked on the zero-data-retention agreement**, which the owner ruled 2026-08-01 is started last; nothing else in Slice V1-I waits on it. | *(Deps: T-319, T-316, the ZDR agreement)*


**Slice Document Status — record state, the ISO code scheme, and what the AI may rely on** *(ruled 2026-08-27, the document-status session → amendments to [ADR-0013](../architecture/adr/0013-supersede-withdraw-states.md), [ADR-0003](../architecture/adr/0003-acceptance-coding.md), [ADR-0041](../architecture/adr/0041-sandbox-versioning-iso-19650.md), [ADR-0045](../architecture/adr/0045-document-ontology-classification-and-relationships.md), [ADR-0011](../architecture/adr/0011-project-library-knowledge-corpus.md) rider, [ADR-0049](../architecture/adr/0049-notifications-and-the-promotion-gate.md); closing `Q-036`. T-383–T-391.)* **In V1**, and **queued behind the Waypoint A corpus floor** — nothing here helps a pilot that cannot yet load documents or read a PDF. Four axes get one word each, three of them adopted from ISO 19650's 2021 National Annex ([the digest](../reference/iso-19650.md)) and the fourth — **record state** — named as Infora's own, because ISO never needed a way to say *stop relying on this*: a human reads the current revision from a register, an un-withdrawn container grounds silently. **The owner currently has no button at all**, and `superseded` is set nowhere in the codebase.
